name: Rise of the Macedonian Dynasty
summary: Basil I, a Macedonian peasant who rose to co-emperor and murdered his predecessor, founded the Macedonian dynasty in 867. Under his successors, especially Nikephoros II Phokas, John I Tzimiskes, and Basil II, Byzantium reconquered Cilicia, Syria, and Bulgaria. Constantine VII Porphyrogennetos presided over a cultural renaissance that preserved classical learning. The dynasty marks the high point of Byzantine medieval power.

_quarry.structural_significance: The Macedonian dynasty represents the zenith of medieval Byzantine military and cultural power; the reconquests they achieved took centuries to lose.

sources_used: Treadgold, A History of the Byzantine State and Society
Magdalino, The Empire of Manuel I Komnenos
